commitResults.messageTitle: Filled in missing fields in AGENTS.md.
Renamed Chatbot from Duke to Steph
Added greeting and exit messages to chatbot
Steph.java: update chatbot to echo commands and exit when command "bye" given
Steph.java: add ability to store text and display it back
Add mark/unmark commands with Task-based tracking
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the raw String task list with a Task class so each task
tracks its own description and done state, enabling mark/unmark.

Dispatch commands via a switch on the first word instead of
if/else "contains" checks.

Validate the task number before indexing into the list
(parseTaskIndex), so an out-of-range, non-numeric, or missing
argument prints a message instead of crashing.

Extract printWrapped/handleList/handleMark/handleAdd helpers to
remove the duplicated LINE-wrapping and mark/unmark logic that
is repeated across branches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ToDo, Deadline, and Event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce ToDo, Deadline, and Event as Task subclasses, each with
its own toString() format, and dispatch todo/deadline/event commands to handlers
that parse the command argument into the fields each type needs.

Deadline and Event arguments are split on their /by, /from,
and /to markers via indexOf rather than String.split(), since
that makes it straightforward to detect a missing marker (index
-1) and reject the command with a usage message instead of
constructing a task with a blank date/time. The default switch
case, which previously added any unrecognized command as a plain
Task, is replaced by the same style of usage-error message.

case, which previously added any unrecognized command as a plain

commitResults.messageTitle: Add test-ui skill for verifying console output
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a skill that runs test/ui-test-plan.md's test cases against the
compiled Steph program: each test case's commands are piped into one
program session, and the response after each command is checked
against the recorded expected output.

Comparing raw console output by hand doesn't scale past a couple of
commands and is easy to eyeball-pass on a subtly wrong string. The
runner script (scripts/run_ui_tests.py) does exact comparison instead,
splitting captured stdout into per-command blocks using the program's
own delimiter line so no test-specific parsing logic has to track
Steph's output format separately.

A `record` mode runs commands for real and prints ready-to-paste
Command/Expected-output blocks, so expected output always comes from
an actual run rather than being hand-typed -- a hand-typed block just
encodes a guess, and guesses that are wrong make a test lie in
whichever direction the mistake points

On a mismatch the runner stops immediately rather than continuing
through the rest of the test case or later cases, since a test case's
commands share state (e.g. `mark 1` depends on the `todo` before it),
so continuing past a wrong output would just cascade into more
failures that don't add information.

Seed the plan with six cases covering todo/deadline/event creation,
mark/unmark, and the two existing error paths (missing `/by`, unknown
command), each captured from a real run rather than typed by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require test-ui after every source change
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a Testing section to AGENTS.md instructing that after any change
under src/main/java, test/ui-test-plan.md is updated if the change
affects console output, and the test-ui skill is run to confirm the
plan still passes.

Without this written down, a future session (or a future me) could
easily ship a change to command parsing or output formatting without
re-running the plan, since nothing else in the workflow forces it. The
section also says not to edit the plan to match broken output just to
make it pass -- a failure should be investigated (regression vs. stale
expectation) rather than silenced.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor error handing in Steph.java to use exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Add StephException (a checked exception carrying a user-facing
message) and have handleMark, handleAddToDo, handleAddDeadline, and
handleAddEvent throw it instead of calling printWrapped(...); return;
on invalid input. The unknown-command case in main's switch now
throws it too, instead of printing directly. A single try/catch
around the switch in main is the only place that calls printWrapped
for these errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a "delete <task-number>" command that removes the task at that
1-based position and reports the new task count, reusing the same
parseTaskIndex validation.

Add two test cases to test/ui-test-plan.md: one deleting a task and
confirming the remaining tasks renumber correctly in a following
list, and one confirming an out-of-range delete is rejected with the
same message style as the other commands' validation errors.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace String command dispatch with a Command enum
commitResults.messageBody:
Add Command, an enum of the seven keywords Steph recognizes
(list/mark/unmark/todo/deadline/event/delete), each carrying its
exact keyword text. Steph.main now looks up the keyword via
Command.fromKeyword(...) and switches on the resulting enum instead
of switching on the raw String.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support program restarts within a UI test case
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI test runner runs each test case as a single Steph process,
so it cannot check behavior that depends on the program stopping
and starting again -- which is what the save-to-disk feature needs
tested.

Run each test case in its own temporary working directory, and let
a bare "### Restart" line in the plan split a case into segments
that run as separate processes sharing that directory. In-memory
state resets at the boundary; anything written to ./data/steph.txt
carries over. "record" mode gains a matching RESTART argument.

The per-case working directory also stops test runs from reading or
overwriting the repo's own ./data/steph.txt.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks to disk and reload them on startup
commitResults.messageBody:
The task list lives only in memory, so every task the user adds is
lost when Steph exits.

Add a Storage class that rewrites ./data/steph.txt after every
command that changes the list and reads it back when Steph starts.
Each Task subclass gains a toFileFormat() method next to its
toString(), so a task encodes itself as one line, e.g.
"T | 1 | read book"; Task becomes abstract, since only the concrete
subclasses produce a complete line.

A missing file means "no tasks yet"; an unreadable file or a single
unparseable line is reported but does not stop startup, so a first
run and a hand-edited file both come up cleanly.

Add a "saved and reloaded across restarts" case to the UI test plan
covering all three task types, the done flag, and a change made
after a restart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
Store deadline and event dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and Event hold their dates as plain strings, so "/by
Sunday" and "/by 2019-12-02" are treated the same.

Parse the /by, /from and /to values as java.time.LocalDate (ISO
yyyy-mm-dd) when the task is created, and display them as
"MMM dd yyyy", e.g. Oct 15 2019. A value that isn't a valid date is
rejected with a hint instead of being stored as-is.

The save file now holds ISO dates, so lines written before this
change with free-text dates like "Sunday" no longer parse; they are
skipped on load with the existing warning. Acceptable, since
./data/steph.txt is local, gitignored state.

Update the deadline, event and persistence cases in the UI test
plan to ISO input and formatted output, and add a case for a
rejected date.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-8'
Store deadline and event dates as LocalDateTime
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines and events currently hold a LocalDate, so a task can only
be pinned to a day, not a time of day.

Accept an optional 24-hour time after the date on /by, /from, and
/to, e.g. "deadline return book /by 2019-10-15 1800". A value with
no time is read as midnight, so existing date-only commands and
save files keep working unchanged.

Date-time parsing, storage encoding, and display formatting move
into a new DateTimes helper so the command parser, the save-file
parser, and the Deadline/Event classes share one definition of the
format. Tasks are saved as ISO LocalDateTime ("2019-10-15T18:00"),
which round-trips without a formatter; parseStored can still read the
old date-only form. Display shows the time only when it isn't midnight,
so a date-only task still prints as "Oct 15 2019".

Update the UI test plan: new cases for timed deadlines and events
and for a time surviving a restart, and the refreshed date-format
hint on the parse-error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: bug fix: Keep <...> placeholders in command Javadoc
commitResults.messageBody:
Javadoc treats a doc comment as HTML, so the <task-name> and
<yyyy-mm-dd> placeholders in the handleAddDeadline / handleAddEvent
comments were parsed as unknown tags and dropped -- the rendered
docs (and IntelliJ's quick-doc popup) showed "Parses  /by   [HHmm]"
with the fields missing.

Wrap the literal command pattern in {@code ...}, which renders it
verbatim in monospace and escapes the angle brackets. Comment-only
change; no behaviour difference and the UI tests are unaffected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract console I/O into a Ui class
commitResults.messageBody:
Steph.main() currently owns every System.out.println and the
Scanner on System.in, mixed in with the command loop and the
command handlers. That makes the presentation (the ____ dividers,
the banner, the greeting) impossible to change without editing
command logic, and impossible to swap for a non-console front end
later.

Move all of it into a new Ui class: showWelcome / showGoodbye /
showMessage / showError / showLoadingError for output, and
hasNextCommand / readCommand / close for input. Steph no longer
imports Scanner or names System.out; each command handler takes a
Ui parameter alongside the task list it already received.

This is a pure relocation -- the console output is byte-for-byte
unchanged and the UI test plan passes as-is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract the task list into a TaskList class
commitResults.messageBody:
Every command handler and Storage.save() currently receive the raw
ArrayList<Task> straight from main(), so the list's representation
and its bounds handling are spread across Steph instead of living
with the data.

Add a TaskList class that owns the list and exposes just what the
commands need: add, get, remove (returning the removed task), size,
and an unmodifiable asList() view for saving. Steph's handlers take
a TaskList instead of an ArrayList; delete no longer does get then
remove.

Storage stays unaware of TaskList: save() now takes List<Task> and
load() still returns a plain list, with TaskList bridging the two
via asList(). The constructor copies the tasks it's given, and
asList() hands back an unmodifiable view, so nothing outside the
class can mutate the list behind its back.

Behaviour is unchanged and the UI test plan passes as-is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract input parsing into a Parser class
commitResults.messageBody:
Steph does its own text wrangling: the keyword/argument split in
main(), parseTaskIndex(), and the /by, /from, /to slicing and
empty-checks scattered through the handleAdd* handlers. Recognising
what the user typed is spread across the whole file.

Add a Parser class that owns all of it -- parseCommand,
parseArguments, parseTaskIndex, and parseToDo / parseDeadline /
parseEvent -- returning a value or throwing StephException with a
message ready to show. The command loop is now
parseCommand -> parseArguments -> switch -> act, and the three
one-line handleAdd* methods collapse into the switch.

One control-flow change: parseTaskIndex now throws from Parser
instead of returning -1 for the caller to check, matching how every
other Parser method reports bad input. It takes the command word as
an argument so the error can still name mark / unmark / delete.

The messages the user sees are byte-for-byte unchanged and the UI test
plan passes as-is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give Steph a constructor and a run() method
commitResults.messageBody:
Steph is still all-static: main() creates the Ui, Storage, and
TaskList as local variables, runs the command loop, and hands them
to every handler as parameters. Nothing about the program can be
built or inspected without running main() start to finish.

Add ui, storage, and tasks as fields, a Steph(String filePath)
constructor that wires them together and loads the saved tasks, and
a run() method holding the loop. main() is now one line:
new Steph("./data/steph.txt").run(). The handlers become instance
methods that read the fields, so their signatures drop back to just
the command argument.

All three fields are final -- each is assigned exactly once in the
constructor. tasks is worked out in a local first and assigned once
after the load's try/catch, rather than assigning the field in both
branches.
